subject: humanities
passage: George Frideric Handel composed much of his music at great speed. Written in only about three weeks in the summer of 1741, ______ The piece soon became one of the most frequently performed works in English choral music.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: the first performance of Messiah took place in Dublin in April 1742.
choices.B: Dublin hosted the first performance of Messiah in April 1742.
choices.C: Handel first presented Messiah in Dublin in April 1742.
choices.D: his oratorio Messiah was first performed in Dublin in April 1742.

explanation.why: The opening phrase "Written in only about three weeks" describes the piece of music, so the music must be the subject right after the comma. Only choice D makes "his oratorio Messiah" the subject.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The subject here is "the first performance," but a performance is not written; the music is.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The subject here is "Dublin," but a city was not written in three weeks.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The subject here is "Handel," so the sentence wrongly says that Handel was written in three weeks.
explanation.D: Correct. "His oratorio Messiah" is the thing that was written, and it directly follows the modifier.
